$comment: Canonical matn identities for the hadith narrations the Golden Set requires. A group names one narration (`same-report`) or one ruling stated by different narrations (`same-ruling`); its members are the corpus rows that carry it through another chain. Every group states its `rationale`, because the two claims are not interchangeable: `same-report` means one matn through different chains and is what citation validity may accept; `same-ruling` means one instruction where wording, chain or companion differ, and only the reported identity-satisfied figure reads it — the exact-address gate never does. A label outside every group is its own identity, so it can never match another. A label may be claimed once per relation (a canonical may anchor both kinds of group); two groups of one relation may not share a label. Owner-signed gate data: adding a group or a member changes what citation validity accepts or what the reported figure counts.

groups.rationale: One report — the Prophet's wudu, shown and described — narrated through different chains; wording differs, the operative content does not.
One instruction — eat with the right hand — narrated through different chains; the members state one operative rule.
One report — cleanliness is half of faith — narrated through different chains; the matn is one statement.
One report of the Prophet combining Maghrib and Isha while travelling, narrated through different chains; the members carry the same account, not merely the same ruling.

One report from Ibn Abbas — Allah obligated a sadaqah from wealth, taken from the rich and returned to the poor — carried by four collections under different numbers; the matn and the lower chain are one account.

Bukhari 1108 and Nasai 598 state the same ruling — combining Maghrib and Isha while travelling — under different chains (Anas vs Ibn Umar/Nafi') and different wording. They are not one report, so the exact-address gate does not read this group.

One instruction — gold and silk are prohibited to the men of this ummah and permitted to its women — narrated from different companions through different chains. The required 5144 states the prohibition without the prayer setting, so the relation is the ruling, not one report.
